statement.p: Use the Chain Rule to calculate the partial derivatives
Express your answer in terms of the independent variables u,v

static.solution: g(x,y)=\cos\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right) are \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{x}}=-2x\sin\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right) \quad \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{y}}=-2y\sin\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right) The partial derivatives of x,y and z with respect to s are \frac{\partial{x}}{\partial{u}}=2 \quad \frac{\partial{x}}{\partial{v}}=1 \frac{\partial{y}}{\partial{u}}=-3 \quad \frac{\partial{y}}{\partial{v}}=-1 We use the Chain Rule to find the following derivative: \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{u}}= \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{x}}\frac{\partial{x}}{\partial{u}}+ \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{y}}\frac{\partial{y}}{\partial{u}} =-\left(4x-6y\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)= =-\left(26u+10v\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(13u^{2}+2v^{2}+10uv\right) \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{v}}= \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{x}}\frac{\partial{x}}{\partial{v}}+ \frac{\partial{g}}{\partial{y}}\frac{\partial{y}}{\partial{v}} =-\left(2x-2y\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)= =-\left(4v+10u\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(13u^{2}+2v^{2}+10uv\right)
